title: Loss of consortium claims - an underused head of compensation
p1:
A serious injury does not only affect the person holding the medical reports. Sometimes, the hidden impact falls on the person standing beside them.

Many people never claim for that loss.
p2: A common misconception is that compensation only covers medical bills, lost income, or physical pain. In many legal systems, a spouse or close family member may also have a claim for the loss of companionship, support, affection, or the normal relationship they once shared.
p3:
This is known as a loss of consortium claim. It recognises that an injury can change a relationship, not just a person's health. The surprising part? Many eligible claims are overlooked because people simply do not know this head of compensation exists.

A practical step after a serious injury is to look beyond immediate financial losses and consider every way life has changed for the affected family.
conclusion: Have you come across a case where the impact on a family relationship was overlooked during a compensation claim?
